# Module `qt`

qt - Qt5 Widgets native GUI, wrapped as an opaque-Int surface.

A small, deterministic subset of Qt5 Widgets for native-window programs. The
C++ QApplication/QWidget/QLabel object model stays in the runtime
(`__vyb_qt_*` shims in `runtime/vyb_qt_bridge.cpp`); Vyb sees only Int
handles (qintptr-sized), Int dimensions, Bool/Int status flags, and String
text. String arguments cross as UTF-8 byte buffers; the title/label-text
getters return owned Strings.

Lifecycle: call qt_init() once. QApplication must live on the main thread,
which is where a Vyb program's main runs. Construction needs a Qt platform -
under X11/xcb with a display, offscreen, etc. On a headless box with neither
a QPA platform nor a $DISPLAY the bridge falls back to the `offscreen`
platform so qt_init() stays deterministic; GUI code is still expected to run
where a GUI is available.

Two event-loop models coexist. The default is *polled*: call
qt_process_events() to pump paint/timer/input events, arm a polled timer with
qt_set_timer(ms) then check qt_timer_fired() (it clears on read), and drain
control signals with qt_event_count/handle/kind/pop (or qt_wait_event). This
stays deterministic under xvfb/offscreen and fits the Int/String FFI.

For a GUI program, qt_run() enters Qt's own native loop (QApplication::exec())
and dispatches queued control events into the handler registered with
qt_on_event(fn(handle, kind)); stop it from a handler with qt_run_stop() (whose
GUI survives) or qt_quit() (full teardown after the loop returns). Background
asyncs keep running on their worker threads and their enqueued results reach
the handler through the same queue-draining loop.

An optional web surface (`qt_web_*`, QWebEngineView) sits on top of Widgets and
is only usable when QtWebEngine is linked into the build (CMake finds
Qt5WebEngineWidgets). With QtWebEngine absent the surface resolves to stub
shims: qt_web_create() returns 0 and the other qt_web_* calls return their
documented defaults, so web-capable programs degrade gracefully. Loading a URL
is asynchronous; loadFinished/titleChanged/loadProgress enqueue the shared
QtEvent kinds and flow through the same qt_on_event / qt_event_* dispatch.

Most operations are T?-shaped (see the docs/FEATURE_STATUS conventions). The
handle/creator functions (qt_*_create, qt_vbox/qt_hbox/qt_grid, qt_menubar,
qt_menu_add, qt_action_add, qt_toolbar_create, qt_tabs_add, qt_dlg_*) return
Int?: an absent value means the handle allocation failed (the bridge returned
0); a present Int?(h) is the live handle. The op-status functions (qt_quit,
qt_process_events, qt_set_timer, the set_*/add/close/load/navigation helpers)
return Bool?: an absent value means the operation failed (the bridge returned
-1, e.g. a bad/0/stale handle or no QApplication); present Bool?(true) means
it succeeded.

Data getters: qt_init/qt_active/qt_window_visible/qt_timer_fired are Bool, and
qt_window_title, qt_*_text/url/count/value/current/index return their data with
a "found nothing"/default value (they report data, not op status). The dimension
getters -- qt_window_width/qt_window_height, qt_screen_width/qt_screen_height,
qt_screen_dpi -- return Int?: present holding the measurement, absent on a bad
window handle or when no screen is available. qt_run returns the exit code;
qt_wait_event returns a Bool.

Modal dialog results are native optionals too: qt_msg_question returns Int?
(present holding 1 for Yes / 0 for No, absent when the GUI is not running), and
the modal pickers qt_file_open/qt_file_save/qt_dir_select plus qt_dlg_selected
return String? via lossless opt intrinsics (present-empty on user cancel, absent
on no-GUI / no-result-yet) -- so a user cancel is never conflated with failure.

| [`qt_window_hide`](#sym-qt_window_hide) | fn |  | Hide (unmap) the window. Returns `Bool?` -- present on success, absent on a bad handle. |
| [`qt_window_resize`](#sym-qt_window_resize) | fn |  | Resize to (width, height) pixels. Returns `Bool?` -- present on success, absent on a bad handle. |
| [`qt_window_set_title`](#sym-qt_window_set_title) | fn |  | Set titlebar text. Returns `Bool?` -- present on success, absent on a bad handle. |
| [`qt_window_show`](#sym-qt_window_show) | fn |  | Show (map) the window. Returns `Bool?` -- present on success, absent on a bad handle. |
| [`qt_window_title`](#sym-qt_window_title) | fn |  | Current titlebar text (String); "" on a bad handle. |
| [`qt_window_visible`](#sym-qt_window_visible) | fn |  | true while window `w` is visible, else false. |
| [`qt_window_width`](#sym-qt_window_width) | fn |  | Content width in pixels. Returns `Int?` -- present holding the width, absent on a bad handle. |
